97f6350bcdb6ae809bb4c99c51c8af63f0875447.teaches: Enjoyment lives in a diagonal band where challenge and skill rise together; too much challenge is anxiety, too little is boredom.
97f6350bcdb6ae809bb4c99c51c8af63f0875447.alt: Challenge plotted against player skill: a diagonal flow channel runs between anxiety above it and boredom below it.
97f6350bcdb6ae809bb4c99c51c8af63f0875447.credit: Redrawn after Csikszentmihalyi (1990); see Schell ch. 11

6ab846ff41b2a38243f370d616110b208dbf4cfb.teaches: The flow channel refines into eight states, so a game can fail in more ways than 'too hard' and 'too easy'.
6ab846ff41b2a38243f370d616110b208dbf4cfb.alt: Eight states arranged by challenge and skill, with flow at high challenge and high skill and apathy at low both.

43c67c45dc1e4c1282a2df0eaf0e969b1fabbab5.teaches: Games can serve needs at every level, but a game that fails a lower need cannot deliver a higher one.
43c67c45dc1e4c1282a2df0eaf0e969b1fabbab5.alt: Five bands of human need from physiological up to self-actualisation, each with the kind of play that serves it.
43c67c45dc1e4c1282a2df0eaf0e969b1fabbab5.credit: After Maslow (1943); the pyramid is a later convention, not his

2904c705cb82a791dda6298509f59d6bc2fece8a.teaches: Players divide by whether they act or interact, and whether they are oriented to other players or to the world.
2904c705cb82a791dda6298509f59d6bc2fece8a.alt: Four player types on two axes: acting against interacting, and oriented to players against oriented to the world.
2904c705cb82a791dda6298509f59d6bc2fece8a.credit: Redrawn after Bartle (1996); see Fullerton ch. 4

0c3ba95e63f23166e110907a95a9478cfbfe6539.alt: The eight GameFlow elements on the left mapped onto seven GameFlow affordances on the right.
0c3ba95e63f23166e110907a95a9478cfbfe6539.credit: Figure from Sweetser & Ozdowska (2024), GameFlow Affordances, CHI EA '24, doi:10.1145/3613905.3650887 — reproduced by permission
0c3ba95e63f23166e110907a95a9478cfbfe6539.permission: Copyright is held by the authors, not ACM (the paper's notice reads '© 2024 Copyright held by the owner/author(s)' and carries no CC licence). Penny Kyburz (Sweetser), as an author and the course convenor, gave permission to publish it on this site, 2026-09-22.

d4f009b761fbbbf0564cfde41c6946fac4556b6e.teaches: Dramatic tension builds to a single climax and resolves; game stories borrow the shape.
d4f009b761fbbbf0564cfde41c6946fac4556b6e.alt: Tension over time rising from exposition through rising action to a climax, then falling to a denouement.

6654d4d9c213d9aebc2396bffbffb673db5f2676.teaches: A good experience hooks quickly, then alternates rise and release with each peak higher than the last.
6654d4d9c213d9aebc2396bffbffb673db5f2676.alt: Interest over time: an early hook, then alternating peaks and troughs each higher than the last, to a climax and release.
6654d4d9c213d9aebc2396bffbffb673db5f2676.credit: Redrawn after Schell ch. 16; beats are our own

11de703cdb416cf51e045364e297460a2fabd16a.teaches: The interest curve is fractal: the same shape governs a whole game, one level and one encounter.
11de703cdb416cf51e045364e297460a2fabd16a.alt: The same interest curve shown at three scales: the whole game, one level and one encounter.

d4487ce0f678c1d99f369bb982e70108f0510831.teaches: Playcentric design is a loop, and problems found on test send you back to generating ideas rather than forward.
d4487ce0f678c1d99f369bb982e70108f0510831.alt: A four-stage loop: generate ideas, formalise, test, evaluate, with problems found feeding back to generate.

f43aaf77f1a0b70ac6d660676ec60c5295221f9a.teaches: Iterations get more numerous, shorter and cheaper as a project moves from concept towards launch.
f43aaf77f1a0b70ac6d660676ec60c5295221f9a.alt: A timeline from concept to launch, with design iterations shown as circles that grow more numerous and smaller.
f43aaf77f1a0b70ac6d660676ec60c5295221f9a.credit: After Fullerton ch. 1; redesigned as a timeline

31160cfeb37784ad686053fd139a70f90c0d619e.teaches: A loop is a closed cycle of mental model, action, rules and feedback that the player can repeat indefinitely.
31160cfeb37784ad686053fd139a70f90c0d619e.alt: A closed cycle: mental model leads to action, action to rules, rules to feedback, feedback back to mental model.

814805c35a8dcbb05aa794cbc3c91fc748e1f7e6.teaches: An arc runs the same four stages once and then is exhausted; that is what makes it different from a loop.
814805c35a8dcbb05aa794cbc3c91fc748e1f7e6.alt: The same four stages as an open chain that ends once exhausted, rather than closing into a cycle.

7dc58cf22d0fba3c1f1241fe5e5e6293c9465854.teaches: The player never touches the game world directly; every action and every response passes through the interface.
7dc58cf22d0fba3c1f1241fe5e5e6293c9465854.alt: The player reaches the game world only through physical input, a virtual interface and physical output, numbered in a loop.

0a476edc19ecf6c5eccbcadff2cfe6a833933f22.teaches: A game has three layers of rule: the abstract system, what players actually do, and the unwritten etiquette.
0a476edc19ecf6c5eccbcadff2cfe6a833933f22.alt: Foundational rules are expressed as operational rules and performed as play, which behavioural rules also shape.
0a476edc19ecf6c5eccbcadff2cfe6a833933f22.credit: Redrawn after Parlett, via Salen & Zimmerman (2004)

eef9ffb0856b6710484f589d02667604d1b3760d.teaches: Who competes or cooperates with whom is a design choice, and there are only a handful of basic shapes.
eef9ffb0856b6710484f589d02667604d1b3760d.alt: Seven player interaction patterns drawn with dots for players and rings for the game, from solo play to team competition.
eef9ffb0856b6710484f589d02667604d1b3760d.credit: After Fullerton ch. 3; redrawn with our own notation

48a3323901dfcc466cc112890f81ca91f87bbc88.teaches: A small state machine with a few transitions produces behaviour players read as intelligence.
48a3323901dfcc466cc112890f81ca91f87bbc88.alt: A state machine for a Pac-Man ghost: in base, chasing, fleeing, flashing and eyes returning to base, with the events between them.
48a3323901dfcc466cc112890f81ca91f87bbc88.credit: After the observable behaviour of Pac-Man (Namco, 1980)

22488afbc6ad8e83d7eea5081014e923a0e55616.teaches: Intransitive balance: every option beats two others and loses to two, so no option dominates.
22488afbc6ad8e83d7eea5081014e923a0e55616.alt: Five options where each beats two of the others and loses to the remaining two, so none dominates.
22488afbc6ad8e83d7eea5081014e923a0e55616.credit: After Kass & Bryla's five-way rock-paper-scissors; see Fullerton ch. 10

0ea46f2ebfdd1d5165ec3599d975ef32fcd03673.credit: Paraphrased from the twelve principles, agilemanifesto.org

0f0ea95f182f319c32f9106da53b39802b025e00.note: A full page of Fullerton's own playtest questions (fig. 9.10, p. 300). Reproducing it verbatim is a substantial excerpt -- paraphrase a few per category and cite the page.

73ab7ce97e06fc6cf2c1c637c36a8f235cbadf0f.alt: Centipede: a field of mushrooms with the player's shooter at the bottom of a single fixed screen.
73ab7ce97e06fc6cf2c1c637c36a8f235cbadf0f.shows: a single-screen game where each 'level' is a variation in difficulty, not a new space

8084ccd8271250174c4072fe37f87758cfccfdde.shows: the same point: one screen, escalating waves

e6062349e9f42174ccf8024be1e811a8258bdc77.alt: Pac-Man: the single maze, with Pac-Man, the ghosts and the dots that every level reuses.
e6062349e9f42174ccf8024be1e811a8258bdc77.shows: one maze reused for every level

c61934614be3c8bd07370852af32fd2c5c6a15ca.alt: A StarCraft map seen from above: terrain, resource patches and the routes between bases.
c61934614be3c8bd07370852af32fd2c5c6a15ca.shows: an RTS level is a map plus a set of objectives

363b45972049b1c9fbc39f81829b9d7158311d54.alt: A packed stadium seen from the stands, the pitch lit below.
363b45972049b1c9fbc39f81829b9d7158311d54.credit: credit to be set when the replacement is sourced
363b45972049b1c9fbc39f81829b9d7158311d54.shows: a sports game's 'level' is the stadium and the opposing team -- a stock photograph of a stadium, replaceable with any freely-licensed one

41f056f5fded0966f1883c6d4110df798fc10a42.alt: Half-Life 2: a crashed helicopter in a rocky outdoor area, the player's shotgun in view.
41f056f5fded0966f1883c6d4110df798fc10a42.shows: level separation: a distinct outdoor area with its own gameplay

644a4057d8fbe9e960ee4a9132b68cd5b9adff86.alt: Half-Life 2: a coastal shack and rubble, approached along a linear route.
644a4057d8fbe9e960ee4a9132b68cd5b9adff86.shows: level order and pacing across a linear chapter

1a48ca5b665b70de26e7cd3cde91c4daacb73db3.alt: Concept art of a ruined city street beneath a suspension bridge.
1a48ca5b665b70de26e7cd3cde91c4daacb73db3.credit: credit to be set when the replacement is sourced
1a48ca5b665b70de26e7cd3cde91c4daacb73db3.shows: concept art of a ruined city -- UNIDENTIFIED, confirm with Penny or substitute

773b85e9e4325c9b4f9d8a7383891847c5da948e.alt: Fallout 3: burnt-out houses and a water tower in an open wasteland, a stop sign still standing.
773b85e9e4325c9b4f9d8a7383891847c5da948e.shows: an open world where the level is the whole space

1a6f441d3b579a4446a9c07ad9a953083efdddba.alt: Bastion: a brightly coloured isometric path assembling itself ahead of the player.
1a6f441d3b579a4446a9c07ad9a953083efdddba.shows: level as a composed, hand-built path through a space

45159745da260984c36901bc5f5c64aa58e8026e.alt: Half-Life 2: two characters talking in a workshop, the level built around the scene.
45159745da260984c36901bc5f5c64aa58e8026e.shows: story-centric level design: events and characters carry the level

a5ccb7fdef0acb8771c73d36dfc70d715ce114f9.alt: Left 4 Dead: survivors silhouetted against a lit doorway as infected close in.
a5ccb7fdef0acb8771c73d36dfc70d715ce114f9.shows: levels built for replay and dynamic pacing

7a07badf8ea3857ee70e12a1f74ed0536365fd7b.alt: Burnout: a car crashing at speed on a highway, debris thrown across the track.
7a07badf8ea3857ee70e12a1f74ed0536365fd7b.shows: a racing level is a track

7e91f41c680c4be10c81ca6bbaf8531f5893ffa9.alt: Dead Space: an armoured engineer facing a necromorph in a wrecked corridor.
7e91f41c680c4be10c81ca6bbaf8531f5893ffa9.shows: atmosphere and threat as level content

1fe8947b6c3fe441344786aa0d330374485bbb3a.alt: Pillars of Eternity: an isometric party crossing a stone bridge in an autumn forest.
1fe8947b6c3fe441344786aa0d330374485bbb3a.shows: an isometric level composed as a painting

b687bc073c6b1a1b829c45f3e30d709ce361f188.alt: Tomb Raider: Lara Croft in an icy chamber, ledges and machinery framing the route.
b687bc073c6b1a1b829c45f3e30d709ce361f188.shows: puzzles and traversal as level content -- confirm which title

cbbefcb9b010e9349c02478e471e6b3b759a8a36.alt: Dead Space: figures lunging at the player in a dim, blood-marked room.

dff73f18d2a96bb0eb2d74bdce8a83495f0a74e7.alt: Warcraft III: an army and base on a green map, with the command interface below.
dff73f18d2a96bb0eb2d74bdce8a83495f0a74e7.shows: an RTS level with objectives, base and terrain

8a8f6880e6d1725d9f81b66ed78402711042ea9b.alt: Grand Theft Auto IV: a city street of traffic and police cars, a helicopter overhead.
8a8f6880e6d1725d9f81b66ed78402711042ea9b.shows: an open-world city as a single continuous level

7970c4ed2fb913ca83cc9430217789533f334296.alt: FIFA: a goalmouth scramble in a stadium, the scoreboard in the corner.
7970c4ed2fb913ca83cc9430217789533f334296.shows: sports: the pitch is the level -- confirm which edition

62c8bfa1434b6ba382648c83e448289f6a93cb3b.alt: Medieval II: Total War: the campaign map of Britain and France, armies and settlements labelled.
62c8bfa1434b6ba382648c83e448289f6a93cb3b.shows: balancing a large system: the campaign map and its many interacting values

d43d0c07e5cfc8d8fb27aa23844e1c9437f2500e.alt: A wall of arcade screens showing many games side by side, each with a different viewpoint.
d43d0c07e5cfc8d8fb27aa23844e1c9437f2500e.credit: credit to be set when the replacement is sourced

dde5c4907ee7f8ebffb4b025412989a3344e8ff4.alt: Diablo II: the inventory screen, equipment slots around a character silhouette above a grid of items.
dde5c4907ee7f8ebffb4b025412989a3344e8ff4.shows: an inventory screen as interface design

de7dc82779078a381df885104299f8fe51cefb36.shows: player-controlled difficulty: the player chooses depth
